summary: F09 is implemented across src/ui/state.rs, src/settings.rs, tests/settings.rs, src/ui/state_tests.rs, and docs/architecture/engine.md: the mix ratio is bounded to 1..=99, typed 0 and 100 clamp to 1 and 99, Settings::validate rejects anything outside the band, and the engine contract records the band and the stored-file consequence.

TIMING-MIX-RATE-BOUNDS-CLAMP.evidence: parse_rate_text rounds and clamps to 1..=99 (the reference's MIX_RATE_MIN/MIX_RATE_MAX) and parse_press_rate_text delegates to it, so both percentage boxes clamp typed input; Settings::validate requires 1..=99 with the message updated to 'between 1 and 99'; the mixer slider already clamped to 1..=99. Re-executed evidence: typed_preservation_rates_clamp_to_whole_percent covers 0->1, 1->1, 99->99, 100->99, 101->99, empty->None; both_ratio_boxes_share_the_rate_band proves the two boxes share the parser; an_out_of_range_mix_ratio_clamps_without_leaving_the_mode drives 0 and 100 through Apply and asserts rates 1 and 99 with the mirrored press buffers 99 and 1; invalid_timing_settings_are_rejected covers rejection at 0/100/101 and acceptance at 1/50/99. The contract bullet in docs/architecture/engine.md records the band and that a stored file still holding the old 100 fails validate() whole, per the documented storage policy.

risks: Stored settings written under the released 1..=100 band can hold overlap_preservation_rate = 100; that file now fails Settings::validate and load_from rejects it whole (the documented no-per-field-clamping policy), so the user sees the load error and falls back to defaults until the value is cleared. The contract bullet records this, and a load-path migration would change the documented storage policy, so it needs explicit direction beyond F09.
The runtime shares Settings::validate, so an older UI binary that still sends rate 100 over IPC would now be rejected by the runtime as an invalid draft.
Native on-screen validation was not performed: the acceptance evidence is unit and state-update tests plus the contract document, not a desktop session.
